description:
The Silver Fang isn't just a mount; it’s a legendary companion that helps you tear through the world of Pywel. While it is easily one of the most powerful and visually striking creatures in Crimson Desert, unlocking it is no small feat. It isn't about your taming skills—it’s about your patience. The Silver Fang is locked behind a massive web of faction quests, boss fights, and prerequisites that can take hours to navigate. In this guide, we break down every single quest you need to complete, from the early days of House Roberts to the final showdown in Howling Hollow.

Looking for a step-by-step Crimson Desert walkthrough to find the Silver Fang? We cover the critical "Silence from Afar" quest, how to unlock House Celeste, and the best strategy for defeating the Black Fang and the Silver Fang boss. Whether you are stuck on the House Serkis horse race or trying to figure out how to brew elixirs in the Abandoned Factory, this guide has the answers.

author: IGN
description:
Is Samson: A Tyndalston Story worth playing to scratch that GTA 6 itch while we wait for the real thing? Well, the thing is, it’s not really a Grand Theft Auto clone: it’s arguably far more interesting. But “interesting” and “good” aren’t the same thing. With its roguelike elements and oppressive debt management system, Samson does dare to offer something that GTA rarely does: real stakes. Heart-pounding consequences for failure. A real sense that, at any moment, you could lose everything.

Coming from some of the same minds behind Just Cause and Mad Max, many gamers have been hoping that Samson has the juice, that it could be a decent GTA clone along the lines of Sleeping Dogs or Red Faction Guerrilla: the kind of game that riffs on Rockstar’s signature formula but adds its own unique twist. But Liquid Swords have been very upfront about this: it is a flawed game without the level of polish the audience might expect.

If you'd like to see more of Jim's video features, check out The T
title: Samson's Game-Changing Feature GTA 6 Should Steal

author: IGN
description:
If there was ever a film that was primed to be an asymmetrical horror game, John Carpenter’s Halloween is it. But after spending some time with it at PAX East, what makes Illfonic’s latest stand out isn’t the asymmetrical horror structure: it’s everything around it. Unlike most asymmetrical horror joints, Halloween isn’t just a 1v4 game where Michael takes on a group of Haddonfield residents. It’s the story of the town of Haddonfield, and what happens to that town when Michael Myers walks the streets. I wasn’t just trying to save myself or the other folks I was playing with; I was trying to save the other people in town, too. Previewed by Will Borger

#IGN #Gaming
title: Halloween Cuts Deeper Than Other 4v1 Games | IGN Preview

The film stars Jack Reynor, Laia Costa, May Calamawy, Natalie Grace, with Veronica Falcón. The film is written and directed by Cronin, and produced by James Wan, Jason Blum and John Keville. Cronin is supported behind the camera by a team of sterling film artisans, including director of photography Dave Garbett, production designer Nick Bassett, editor Bryan Shaw, costume designer Joanna Eatwell, music by Stephen McKeon and casting by Terri Taylor and Sarah Domeier Lindo.

In season two, when a young man is stabbed to death at a political rally, rival police officers June Lenker and Daniel Hegarty are forced into an uneasy alliance.
